AWL Agri Business.desc: Formerly Adani Wilmar, AWL is India's largest branded edible-oil player (Fortune oils) and a growing food-staples company with wheat flour, rice, pulses, sugar and ready-to-cook lines. Post the Adani Enterprises stake sale to Wilmar, the business is being repositioned as a pure-play branded-foods franchise with industry-leading distribution depth across 1 million+ outlets. Strategic reset and scale-driven upside have the business assuming coverage at Buy with TP ₹340 (Jeff, 2026/05/19); margin profile is thin and commodity-sensitive but mix is shifting toward value-added foods.

Adani Power.desc: India's largest private-sector thermal power generator with ~18 GW of operating capacity and a roadmap to ~31 GW by FY30E across coal-fired plants in Mundra, Tiroda, Kawai, Udupi, Raipur and Mahan. Earnings volatility has eased as merchant exposure shrinks — 95% of operating capacity is now tied up under long-term PPAs at improving tariffs (Jeff, 2026/05/18). Capacity additions are largely equipment-locked at competitive rates with L&T and BHEL, supporting visibility on 20%+ EBITDA CAGR through FY30 with FCF turning positive by FY30E (Jeff, 2026/05/18).

Afcons Infrastructure.desc: Flagship infrastructure-EPC arm of the Shapoorji Pallonji group, executing marine, urban-metro, hydro, oil & gas, surface-transport and underground projects across India, the Middle East, Africa and South Asia. Strong record on complex, technically-differentiated jobs (sea-link bridges, large-diameter tunnels, hydro caverns) drives an order book usually 3× trailing revenue. 4QFY26 saw muted operating performance with EBITDA down 43% YoY on execution slowdown from West Asia tensions; FY27 outlook hinges on conversion of the ~₹1.8tn pipeline (Nomura, 2026/05/19).

Amber Enterprises.desc: India's largest room-AC contract manufacturer, supplying most major brands (Voltas, Daikin, LG, Samsung, Whirlpool) with finished ACs, components and increasingly electronics. The electronics (PCBA) and railway sub-systems verticals via Sidwal and ILJIN are scaling fast and now anchor the long-term growth story, with timely PCB commissioning a key near-term margin lever (Kotak, 2026/05/18). Near-term margin pressure is largely priced in (CLSA, 2026/05/19); JPM flagged margin pressure and PCB execution delays as the watch items (JP, 2026/05/18).

Anthem Biosciences.desc: Bangalore-based contract research, development and manufacturing organisation serving global innovator pharma and biotech with small molecules, peptides, biologics and fermentation chemistry. Differentiated technology stack (one-stop NCE-to-commercial integration) and a long-tail customer book have delivered industry-leading 30%+ EBITDA margins. JPMorgan first-take cites strong growth with best-in-class margins (JP, 2026/05/20); China+1 thesis and biologics ramp-up underpin the growth case.

Astral.desc: India's #2 CPVC/PVC plumbing-pipes brand with growing presence in adhesives (Resinova), paints, water tanks, valves and bath-ware — pivoting toward a broader building-materials platform. Mar-Q plumbing volumes grew +24% on share gains and channel expansion, though adhesives margin took a near-term hit from raw-material inflation (Jeff, 2026/05/18); JPM noted a marginal EBITDA miss but strong operational metrics and stayed OW (JP, 2026/05/18). CLSA sees the operational performance broadly in line (CLSA, 2026/05/19); long runway from housing under-penetration and the unorganised-to-organised shift.

Avalon Technologies.desc: Vertically-integrated industrial EMS player with manufacturing in India and the US, focused on box-build for power, semiconductor, clean-energy, medical and aerospace customers. Differentiated by end-to-end PCBA-to-system assembly capability and proximity to US OEMs at a moment when nearshoring + AI-driven power capex are accelerating. Nomura's anchor report initiates at Buy with TP ₹1,722, calling out TAM expansion in HVDC, BESS and SPE (Nomura, 2026/05/19).

Avenue Supermarts.desc: Operator of the DMart value-retail chain — India's most efficient hypermarket format with the lowest cost-to-serve in the listed retail universe. Slowed store additions hurt revenue growth in FY24-26, but FY26 saw +85 net new stores and 20% YoY network expansion. Bernstein argues LFL matters more than store growth and the recent LFL slowdown is more cyclical than structural — driven by low staples inflation and quick-commerce disruption in metros (Bern, 2026/05/20).

Bajaj Finserv.desc: Holding company of the Bajaj group's financial-services franchise — Bajaj Finance (consumer lending), Bajaj Allianz Life & General Insurance, and newer ventures in payments, broking and AMC. Jefferies' roadshow feedback flagged core growing well and new ventures near breakeven (Jeff, 2026/05/18). Investor focus has shifted to the new-ventures portfolio and execution on the holdco discount.

Bharat Electronics.desc: Government-owned defence-electronics PSU and India's largest indigenous-radar, communication-systems and electronic-warfare supplier. Order book of ~₹70k cr provides 3-year revenue cover; civilian diversification into homeland security, space, civil aviation and semiconductor packaging widens the addressable market. 4QFY26 was steady with a slight miss on Nomura's estimates (Nomura, 2026/05/19); near-term concerns are around order-inflow lumpiness post the FY24-26 surge.

Bharat Petroleum.desc: India's second-largest oil-marketing company with ~16% market share in fuel retail, plus refining capacity of ~38 mmtpa at Mumbai, Kochi and Bina. 4QFY26 was hit by a big ₹43.5bn impairment charge linked to its upstream subsidiary (CLSA, 2026/05/20); JPM's first take called it a beat marred by BPRL impairment losses (JP, 2026/05/19). Big-ticket projects include the Bina petrochemical complex and city-gas expansion through Bharat Gas Resources.

CMS Info Systems.desc: India's largest cash-management company — ATM cash replenishment, cash-in-transit, retail cash management and managed services for banks. Jefferies' Mar-Q note flagged improving business momentum and the FSS acquisition supporting FY27 growth (Jeff, 2026/05/17). Volume growth is steady; the moat is the unmatched logistics footprint across 25,000+ pin codes.

Carborundum Universal.desc: Murugappa-group leader in abrasives, ceramics and electro-minerals — a key supplier to automotive, infrastructure, energy and electronics OEMs in India and globally via subsidiaries in Russia, South Africa and the US. Kotak sees growth accelerating with loss-making subs on their way out (Kotak, 2026/05/18); long-term thesis is industrial-capex revival and import-substitution in technical ceramics.

Chalet Hotels.desc: K Raheja-promoted luxury and upscale hotel chain operating Marriott, Westin, JW Marriott, Renaissance and Hyatt Regency properties in Mumbai, Bengaluru, Hyderabad and Pune. Kotak flagged a rickety close to FY26 but capacity addition remains strong (Kotak, 2026/05/18); IDBI and Axis remain constructive with Buy ratings on the FY27 pipeline (IDBI, 2026/05/18; Axis, 2026/05/18). Capacity addition pipeline of 800+ keys and the commercial real-estate annuity portfolio add to the growth optionality.

Coforge.desc: Midcap IT services exporter with deep verticals in BFSI, travel & transportation and insurance — and a strategic bet on AI-led platforms (Quasar) and large-deal execution. Acquired Cigniti to build a quality-engineering & AI competency at scale. CLSA highlights bold bets and execution as the differentiation (CLSA, 2026/05/19); margins are in a transitional dip from integration but deal TCV growth leads the midcap pack.

Deepak Nitrite.desc: Integrated specialty-chemicals producer (phenol, acetone, IPA, fuel additives, performance chemicals) with India's only large-scale phenol-acetone complex at Dahej. Kotak cautions that windfall profits on phenol may not last beyond a couple of quarters (Kotak, 2026/05/18); growth focus is shifting to downstream solvents, fluorination chemistry and a polycarbonate JV. The long-run thesis is the China+1 specialty story.

Delhivery.desc: India's largest integrated logistics-tech company — express parcel, part-truckload, full-truckload, supply-chain services and cross-border for e-commerce, D2C and SME shippers. Crossed the FCF-positive milestone in FY26 — Kotak calls it a blockbuster end to a strong year (Kotak, 2026/05/18), JPM headlines simply 'here comes the FCF' (JP, 2026/05/18). PTL is the swing factor for margins; volumes and yields are both inflecting.

Devyani International.desc: India's largest QSR franchisee — operates KFC, Pizza Hut and Costa Coffee stores in India, Nepal, Nigeria and beyond. Aggressive store expansion has driven scale but compressed margins; Kotak's recent note called the latest print 'a welcome relief' on early SSSG recovery (Kotak, 2026/05/17). Net store count is growing 20%+; turnaround in Pizza Hut SSSG is the watch item.

Fusion Finance.desc: Microfinance lender with operations across 22 states and a focus on rural and semi-urban income groups. Asset quality has been pressured by the post-COVID stress cycle in the MFI sector; CLSA flagged 'some improvement' in the latest print on stabilising PAR trends (CLSA, 2026/05/18). Capital position is comfortable post the FY25 fund-raise; the recovery in credit costs is the key earnings lever.

GE Vernova T&D India.desc: Indian subsidiary of GE Vernova's grid-solutions business — power transformers, high-voltage substations, GIS, HVDC and FACTS systems supplied to PGCIL, state utilities and private generators. Beneficiary of the multi-decade transmission cycle in India (renewables integration, HVDC build-out, T&D modernisation). JPM is incrementally positive on the long-term story and raised PT to ₹5,050 (JP, 2026/05/20); Nomura calls the 4QFY26 print exemplary with another upward revision (Nomura, 2026/05/19).

Gland Pharma.desc: India's largest pure-play generic-injectables exporter to US, EU, Canada, Australia and emerging markets — a contract-development and manufacturing platform for sterile injectables. 4QFY26 came in significantly higher than estimates (Nomura, 2026/05/17); Jefferies sees the outlook improving with execution as the key monitorable (Jeff, 2026/05/17). Cenexi (France) sterile-fill ramp and the US business turnaround remain the two execution swing factors.

Global Health (Medanta).desc: Operator of Medanta hospitals in Gurugram, Lucknow, Patna, Indore and Noida — among India's leading tertiary and quaternary care chains with strong oncology, cardiology and transplant programmes. JPM upgraded to OW citing entry into a growth-acceleration phase (JP, 2026/05/18); PL flagged Noida unit ramp-up on track (PL, 2026/05/18). New units (Noida, Patna ramp-up) drive ARPOB and EBITDA leverage.

Hindalco.desc: Aditya Birla group's flagship metals company — India's largest aluminium and copper producer plus the global Novelis platform in flat-rolled aluminium products. Novelis (US) is the swing factor (auto, packaging, aerospace end-markets); the India business is among the lowest-cost aluminium smelters globally. CLSA sees Novelis core earnings strong (CLSA, 2026/05/20) and JPM says Novelis 4Q allays most investor concerns (JP, 2026/05/20); Jefferies flagged another fire-impacted quarter at Novelis Mar-Q (Jeff, 2026/05/19).

Hindustan Aeronautics.desc: India's largest aerospace and defence PSU — designs and manufactures fighter aircraft (Tejas LCA), helicopters (LCH, ALH, LUH), engines, avionics and MRO services. Nomura highlights robust sales-growth visibility given a manufacturing book-bill ratio of 25× (Nomura, 2026/05/18); CLSA notes the backlog is built and execution is now the next leg (CLSA, 2026/05/18). Order book is at a record on the back of large IAF orders (Tejas Mk1A, AMCA prototypes) plus follow-on helicopter contracts.

ICICI Prudential Life Insurance.desc: Joint venture between ICICI Bank and Prudential PLC, among India's largest private life insurers with a balanced ULIP-protection-annuity mix. Bernstein expects the stock under pressure with parent stake sale confirmed (Bern, 2026/05/18); Nomura also flagged Prudential's intent to reduce stake (Nomura, 2026/05/18). Underlying VNB margin and APE growth remain in line with the broader sector.

ITC Hotels.desc: ITC's hotels business demerged into a separate listing — luxury and upper-upscale chain (ITC Grand, ITC Royal, WelcomHotel, Mementos, Storii, Fortune) with 140+ properties across India and select overseas. Jefferies flagged FTA impact driving a weak Mar-Q (Jeff, 2026/05/17). ARR pricing power and asset-light owned-and-managed growth are the long-term levers.

India Macro.desc: Sector notebook covering India macro indicators — CPI, IIP, GDP, fiscal deficit, RBI policy, currency, oil & commodity exposure. Aggregates broker views, RBI/MoSPI releases and the IMF/IFS macro feed used in the News tab snapshot.

India Strategy.desc: Sector notebook collating India-strategy reports from broker research houses — quarterly earnings dissectors, sector rotation calls, model-portfolio changes and valuation frameworks.

Indian Banks.desc: Sector notebook on Indian banking — large private banks (HDFC, ICICI, Axis, Kotak), PSU banks, asset-quality cycle, NIM trajectory, deposit competition and loan-growth mix across retail, SME and corporate.

Indian Cement.desc: Sector notebook on Indian cement — Big-5 consolidation (UltraTech, Ambuja-ACC, Shree, Dalmia, JK), pricing discipline, regional supply-demand, infra/housing demand drivers and clinker capacity additions.

Indian Financials.desc: Sector notebook for India financials — banks, NBFCs, life and general insurance, asset-management and capital-markets businesses. Tracks system credit growth, deposit-LDR dynamics and the BFSI monthly indicators.

Indian Hotels.desc: IHCL operates the Taj, SeleQtions, Vivanta, Ginger and Tree of Life brands across India and key gateway markets — over 200 hotels and a long pipeline of asset-light openings. Jefferies notes April RevPAR growth improving with Goa leading the recovery (Jeff, 2026/05/19). Asset monetisation and the asset-light pipeline are unlocking capital for the next leg of growth.

Indian IT.desc: Sector notebook on Indian IT services — Tier-1 (TCS, Infosys, Wipro, HCL, Tech Mahindra), Tier-2 (Coforge, Persistent, LTIMindtree, Mphasis, LTTS, Cyient) and the discretionary-spend / AI-led-transformation cycle.

Indian Jewellery.desc: Sector notebook on Indian organised jewellery — Titan/Tanishq, Kalyan, Senco, PNG, Joyalukkas — covering gold price cycle, hallmarking regulation, store expansion and the unorganised-to-organised market-share shift.

Indian Oil Corporation.desc: India's largest oil-marketing and refining company — ~30% market share in fuels retail, ~80 mmtpa refining capacity and an extensive cross-country pipeline network. JPM's first take called Mar-Q a beat driven by inventory gains (JP, 2026/05/19); Jefferies sees the valuation favourable (Jeff, 2026/05/19); Nomura ranks IOC its top pick among OMCs (Nomura, 2026/05/19). Capex on petchem (Paradip), green-hydrogen and gas pipelines continues.

Indian Pharmaceuticals.desc: Sector notebook for Indian pharma — generic exporters (Sun, Cipla, Lupin, Aurobindo, Dr Reddy's, Zydus), domestic-formulations leaders (Mankind, Torrent, Alkem) and CDMO/CRO names. Tracks USFDA inspection cadence, GxMeter pricing and India MAT growth.

Indian Steel.desc: Sector notebook on Indian steel — Tata Steel, JSW Steel, SAIL, Jindal Steel & Power, plus regional players. Tracks HRC pricing, coking-coal cycle, capacity additions and import/export dynamics.

Indraprastha Gas.desc: Delhi-NCR's leading city-gas-distribution company — supplies CNG to vehicles and PNG to households, commercial and industrial customers across Delhi, Noida, Greater Noida, Ghaziabad, Karnal and Rewari. CLSA called Mar-Q a margin-led beat (CLSA, 2026/05/19) and IGL is weathering the storm into FY27 (CLSA, 2026/05/20); JPM cautions cost pressures can continue near term (JP, 2026/05/20). Recent CNG price hikes have restored margins (Kotak, 2026/05/19); the medium-term thesis is rising EV substitution in 2W/3W vs CNG growth in 4W and HCV.

JSW Energy.desc: JSW Group's integrated power utility — coal, hydro, solar, wind and a growing battery-storage / green-hydrogen portfolio. Targets ~20 GW operating capacity by FY30, evenly split between renewables and thermal. Jefferies says JSW Energy is moving in the right direction (Jeff, 2026/05/18); CLSA labels the latest acquisition a good deal with caveats (CLSA, 2026/05/20).

KEC International.desc: RPG-group flagship EPC contractor — power-transmission lines, substations, railways, civil, cables and oil & gas pipelines across India, the Middle East, Africa and the Americas. Order book is at a record ~₹363bn but Nomura downgraded to Neutral on persistent weakness in operating performance and soft guidance, TP cut from ₹845 to ₹507 (Nomura, 2026/05/19). Kotak sees recovery as gradual after a weak FY26 (Kotak, 2026/05/18).

KIMS.desc: Krishna Institute of Medical Sciences — South India's leading multi-specialty hospital chain with anchors in Hyderabad and growing presence in Kerala, Karnataka and Maharashtra. Kotak says KIMS is 'still not there yet' on the cluster build-out (Kotak, 2026/05/18); PL is more positive — new clusters in BLR/MUM/KOL to drive growth, BUY with TP ₹800 (PL, 2026/05/19).

MakeMyTrip.desc: India's largest online travel platform — flights, hotels, holidays, bus and rail bookings across MakeMyTrip, Goibibo and redBus. US-listed (NASDAQ); business is sensitive to discretionary travel spend and currency. JPM cut PT to $60 from $110 on near-term Middle East and oil-price headwinds while staying OW (JP, 2026/05/20).

Mankind Pharma.desc: India's #4 pharma company by domestic prescriptions — strongest in chronic therapies (cardiac, anti-diabetic, anti-infective) with mass-market consumer brands (Manforce, Prega News, Gas-O-Fast). Bharat Serums acquisition added the women's health and critical-care portfolio. 4QFY26 saw a revenue miss but margins came in ahead (JP, 2026/05/20).

NHPC.desc: India's largest hydro-power generator — operates 8 GW across 24 stations with another 4-5 GW under construction including the marquee Parbati-II and Subansiri-Lower projects. CLSA's 'worth the wait' thesis: FY26 saw RegEq +25% YoY on new project start-up, but a delay in Parbati-II tariff and Teesta restoration deflated PAT by ~20% (CLSA, 2026/05/18). Kotak flags earnings growth as one-off-driven (Kotak, 2026/05/19).

Nagarjuna.desc: Hyderabad-based mid-cap EPC contractor (also known as NCC Ltd) executing buildings, transport, electrical, irrigation, water and metals projects. CLSA stays cautious — 'still hazy or defensive' (CLSA, 2026/05/18). Order book provides 3-year revenue cover; FY27E caution persists as receivables and working capital remain stretched.

Neogen Chemicals.desc: India's largest bromine-based specialty chemicals producer with a fast-growing organo-lithium and electrolyte-additives portfolio targeting lithium-ion battery supply chains. Kotak's note frames it as 'everything comes to him who hustles while he waits' — capacity expansion programme nearly complete with battery-materials commercial ramp-up the FY27-28 swing factor (Kotak, 2026/05/18).

Orkla India.desc: Indian arm of Norway's Orkla group — owner of MTR Foods (South Indian ready-meals, spices), Eastern Condiments and Rasoi Magic. Recently IPO-listed; growth playbook is premium South Indian foods plus export to the diaspora. JPM's Q4 review flagged volume growth moderating on Kerala distribution reset and weak overseas (JP, 2026/05/20).

Power Grid.desc: State-owned monopoly transmission utility — operates ~178,000 ckm of EHV lines, India's central transmission system. FY26 capex grew +52% to ₹400bn and capitalisation jumped +213% YoY to ₹282bn, exceeding company guidance (Jeff, 2026/05/18). CLSA frames Mar-Q as 'beat beat beat' (CLSA, 2026/05/19); Bernstein sees the print as 'same old' — capex beat, earnings miss (Bern, 2026/05/18); Kotak stays REDUCE with FV ₹295 on stretched valuations (Kotak, 2026/05/18). FY27/28 capex/capitalisation guidance retained, long-term HVDC and GEC opportunity is structurally robust.

Premier Energies.desc: Hyderabad-based integrated solar manufacturer — cells, modules and EPC services with ~5 GW module / 2 GW cell capacity expanding to ~10/5 GW by FY27. Beneficiary of India's PLI programme and rising domestic-content requirements (ALMM/DCR). 4Q operating performance beat estimates (Nomura, 2026/05/18); Jefferies' Mar-26 review flagged 'marginally ahead, strong FY27 outlook' (Jeff, 2026/05/17); JPM sees margins holding up with improved solar outlook positive for the stock (JP, 2026/05/18).

ReNew.desc: US-listed independent power producer — India's largest by operating renewable capacity (>10 GW utility-scale wind + solar) with growing manufacturing (solar PV) and C&I business. Recent fund-raises at compelling valuations highlight asset value vs the depressed listing price. Bernstein flags Q4FY26 execution strong but earnings impacted by curtailment; entire company trades at ~$2bn market cap with the solar-PV manufacturing and C&I businesses alone worth ~$1.8bn at recent transaction valuations (Bern, 2026/05/18).

Restaurant Brands Asia.desc: Master franchisee of Burger King in India and Indonesia — currently undergoing brand-extension into Popeyes (premium chicken QSR). CLSA highlights consistent SSSG growth in the latest print (CLSA, 2026/05/18); Kotak frames it as a 'steady show in India' (Kotak, 2026/05/18). Indonesia continues to be a drag with restructuring in progress.

S H Kelkar and Company.desc: India's leading domestic fragrance & flavour producer — captive serves FMCG, personal-care and home-care customers across India and ~50 export markets. Kotak flags margins remaining under pressure with an FY2028 turnaround story (Kotak, 2026/05/18).

SJVN.desc: Central PSU operating ~2.1 GW of hydro power across Himachal, Bhutan and Nepal — expanding into thermal, solar, wind and pumped-storage with a ~25 GW target by FY30. CLSA cautions SJVN is 'not out of the woods yet' (CLSA, 2026/05/19); project execution at scale remains the swing factor.

Siemens Energy India.desc: Demerged Siemens India energy business — high-voltage T&D, gas turbines, generators and digital-grid solutions. JPM sees export growth as a key positive but turbine and HVDC concerns keep them at Neutral (JP, 2026/05/18). Beneficiary of India's transmission cycle and global Western-OEM diversification.

Steel Authority of India.desc: India's largest steel PSU — integrated plants at Bhilai, Bokaro, Rourkela, Durgapur, IISCO and special-steels plants. JPM flagged Q4FY26 earnings beat and debt-reduction positive with volume growth soft until FY31 (JP, 2026/05/18); IDBI maintains Sell with TP ₹158 on the soft volume trajectory (IDBI, 2026/05/18). Expansion at Bhilai and other plants is staggered.

TCS.desc: Tata Consultancy Services — India's largest IT exporter and a top-3 global IT services firm with deep banking, retail, manufacturing and life-sciences verticals. Kotak's CFO meeting notes: only ~5% of enterprises are in mature AI stages, revenue-deflation risk is real if pricing fails to pivot from effort-based to outcome-based, vendor consolidation is high with TCS the net gainer; BUY maintained with FV ₹3,100 (Kotak, 2026/05/18). Margins face larger productivity commitments, wage hikes and M&A drag.

Tata Steel.desc: Tata group's integrated steelmaker — India operations (~21 mmtpa), Europe (Netherlands ~7 mmtpa, UK transitioning to EAF), plus mining and downstream-products businesses. Nomura's Mar-Q EBITDA beat driven by stronger realisations — domestic HRC prices rose ~14% q-q (Nomura, 2026/05/18); CLSA sees the print as operationally in line (CLSA, 2026/05/18); Jefferies expects more margin expansion ahead (Jeff, 2026/05/16). Netherlands going-concern overhang persists; capex on Kalinganagar Phase-II nearing completion.

Timken.desc: Indian subsidiary of US Timken Co — supplies tapered roller, cylindrical and spherical bearings to railways (LHB coaches, Vande Bharat), trucks, off-highway equipment and process industries. Kotak flags 'an improved performance' with rising railway-capex tailwinds (Kotak, 2026/05/19); export growth is the optionality.

United Spirits.desc: Diageo India's listed spirits business — owns Royal Challenge, Signature, McDowell's, plus distributes Johnnie Walker and other Diageo brands locally. JPM frames it as 'mixing it right for FY27' — premiumisation + the '3 Indias' playbook underpin double-digit growth aspirations (JP, 2026/05/18); CLSA warns of margin headwinds ahead (CLSA, 2026/05/18); Nomura sees 1H27 volumes/margins under pressure but the medium-term story intact (Nomura, 2026/05/18); Kotak sees premiumisation set to accelerate further (Kotak, 2026/05/18).

Uno Minda.desc: Tier-1 auto-components supplier — switches, lighting, horns, EV power-electronics (drive-units, BMS, motors), seat assemblies and infotainment to OEMs in India and globally. Nomura notes EV order wins keep growth visibility high but cuts TP to ₹1,494 from ₹1,513 on near-term cost pressure (Nomura, 2026/05/18); Jefferies says growing well but flags near-term margin pressure (Jeff, 2026/05/18); Kotak labels Mar-Q a 'lackluster quarter' (Kotak, 2026/05/18); CLSA more positive — 'another steady quarter' (CLSA, 2026/05/18). FY27 EBITDA margin guidance 11% ±50bp.

Vodafone Idea.desc: India's #3 wireless operator (~22% revenue share) — capex-constrained relative to Jio/Bharti; absence of bank funding remains the binding constraint. JPM stays UW with PT ₹9 — 'not out of the woods yet' (JP, 2026/05/19); CLSA more constructive on AGR gain and promoter equity infusion of ₹47.3bn via warrants at ₹11/share (CLSA, 2026/05/19); Kotak sees subscriber base stabilising but turnaround as a tall ask (Kotak, 2026/05/19). ARPU growth and tariff hikes are the swing factors.

Zee Entertainment.desc: India's largest listed broadcaster — Zee TV linear network plus Zee5 streaming and a regional-language portfolio. CLSA flags Mar-Q EBITDA loss highlighting the structural ad-market pressure on linear TV (CLSA, 2026/05/20); cost-out programme and digital-monetisation pivot are the key levers.

Zydus Lifesciences.desc: Ahmedabad-based generic pharma — large US generics business, growing domestic-formulations franchise (Zydus Wellness consumer-healthcare), biosimilars and an emerging NCE pipeline. Jefferies cites strong Mar-Q and FY27 guidance, maintains BUY (Jeff, 2026/05/19); Nomura calls 4QFY26 ahead of estimates (Nomura, 2026/05/19); JPM sees good execution and visible pipeline but upside priced in (JP, 2026/05/20).
